key_insight: For CO2-to-CH4 conversion in perovskite oxides, the unoccupied TM 3d-band center, charge-transfer energy, and especially the W3d/W2p bandwidth ratio are the strongest negative descriptors of activity.
engineering_relevance: A simple electronic-structure metric can guide high-throughput screening of perovskite catalysts, helping prioritize compositions likely to improve CO2 reduction performance.
method: Analyzed six band-center/bandwidth descriptors for correlation with CH4 activity.
Used parametric brute-force searching (BFS) to derive explicit fitting equations.
Applied the selected equation to screen 24 La-based double perovskites.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports negative correlations for key descriptors and identifies La2CoGaO6, La2CoAlO6, and Ti-containing compositions as promising candidates from the screening.
watch_item: The descriptor-activity trends are qualitative-to-semiquantitative, so predicted candidates still need experimental validation under realistic catalytic conditions.
paper_title: Electronic Structure Descriptors for CO$_2$ Conversion Activity in Perovskite Oxides
